Jacksonville website design starts with a map. The city covers about 747 square miles of land, and with its rivers and marshes added in, about 874 square miles in total. A customer in Mandarin, one in Arlington and one at the Beaches all say they live in Jacksonville, and they can be a long drive apart. A site that only says "serving Jacksonville" leaves every one of them wondering whether you will come.

To be clear for searchers, this page is about Jacksonville, Florida. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds each site by hand from East Texas, shows you a free demo first, and charges a printed one-time price.

Jacksonville website design for a city you cannot cross on a lunch break

People often call Jacksonville the biggest city in the lower 48 by area. A Jacksonville Today fact-check found that claim holds for total area, water included, while Greeley County, Kansas, which merged with the city of Tribune in 2009, has slightly more land. Either way, the scale is the point. On a city this size, the word "Jacksonville" on its own tells a customer and Google very little about where you actually work.

Think about an air conditioning company based on the Westside. Its crew can reach Orange Park in Clay County quickly, but a call from Ponte Vedra might mean a long drive each way. If the website lists every corner of the city equally, the owner pays for that in wasted trips and unhappy callers.

A better site says where you go, how far, and whether there is a trip charge outside that zone. It might have one page for the Westside and Orange Park and another for the Southside, each written about that area, so the right customer finds the right page.

Where your customers say they live

Residents rarely say "Duval County." They say the name of their part of town, and good web design Jacksonville FL customers respond to uses those same names. These are the ones worth putting on your pages, where they are true for your business:

Area people nameWhat a page for it should answer
Riverside and AvondaleParking, hours, and whether your work suits the age and type of buildings you will find there.
San MarcoDo you come to the neighborhood, or is your shop close enough to visit?
Southside and MandarinResponse time from where your trucks start the day, and the main roads you cover.
ArlingtonWhether you cross the river to reach it, and how quickly.
NorthsideService hours and whether you take commercial jobs as well as homes.
The BeachesTrip charges, weekend availability and how to book ahead.
Orange Park and Clay CountyA plain statement that you work outside the city line, if you do.

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. A page that honestly names the area you serve helps Google match you to a nearby searcher. Pro includes ten city pages written this way; owners covering more ground can use Agency, which starts with keyword research across the whole service area.

Navy families find you from scratch

Jacksonville is a Navy town. The City of Jacksonville lists NAS Jacksonville, Naval Station Mayport and nearby Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay in Georgia among the installations employing thousands of active duty, reserve and civilian workers. Citing a January 2024 Florida summary, the city puts Duval County's military-related economic impact at about $9.1 billion, roughly 17 percent of the county economy, with about 68,060 jobs. Local estimates, including a U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development market study, have long put the number of people leaving the military who settle in the area each year at around 3,000.

Families on orders arrive without a neighbor to ask for a dentist, a pet sitter, a mechanic or a moving cleaner. They search on a phone, often before the moving truck shows up. A site that serves them well does a few simple things:

  • Says which bases and parts of town you are near, in plain words.
  • Explains how to book and what a first visit costs, so a newcomer can decide without a phone call.
  • Mentions any military discount you really offer, and leaves it out if you do not.
  • Loads fast and reads well on a phone, because that is where the search happens.

Website development in Jacksonville, and when you need it

Some owners search for "website development Jacksonville" when what they want is a website. The difference is simple. Design and writing decide what the site says and how it looks. Development is building software: logins, databases, booking engines tied to your own systems, large online stores.

Most local service businesses need the first kind. We build and host the site, write each page, connect the contact form to your email, and set up titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema so search engines can read it.

If you need the second kind, we will say so. Online stores and custom software are not in our packages, and a firm that builds them is the better choice.

Two programs worth a Jacksonville owner's time

Florida SBDC at UNF

The Florida Small Business Development Center at the University of North Florida offers consulting by appointment at little or no cost, paid for by federal SBA funds and contributions from the university, the City of Jacksonville and other partners. It serves 18 North Florida counties, including Duval, Clay, Nassau and St. Johns, with satellite centers on the Northside and Westside.

JSEB certification

The city's Jacksonville Small and Emerging Business program certifies small firms for city contracting. The business must be in Duval County and its owners must live in Duval, Baker, Clay, Nassau or St. Johns County, along with rules on net worth, ownership and control. The city holds JSEB certification training on the second Tuesday of each month.

Common questions

How much does Jacksonville website design cost?

It ranges widely, and many firms quote only after a sales call. Our prices are printed: $497 for the 5-page Starter, $997 for Pro with ten pages plus ten city pages, and $1,997 for Agency, which starts with keyword research across your service area. Each is a one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

What should I look for in a Jacksonville web design company?

A written price, a clear answer on who writes the words, who owns the domain and the site, and what hosting costs after launch. Ask to see something built for your business before you pay. We are one person, not a team: Maurice Johnson writes and builds each site himself and shows you a free demo first. We have no office in Jacksonville.

Is this page about Jacksonville, Florida or Jacksonville, North Carolina?

Jacksonville, Florida, on the St. Johns River in Duval County. Jacksonville, North Carolina is a different city with a similar name, and search results sometimes mix the two. If your business is in North Carolina, our packages still apply, but the local details on this page do not.

Can one website cover Orange Park, St. Johns County and the Beaches?

Yes, as long as you really work there. The better approach is a separate page for each area, written about that place, rather than one long list of town names. Pro includes ten city pages. Agency researches your whole service area first and builds a page for each town and service combination worth having, usually 30 to 60, delivered in waves.

Do you offer website development in Jacksonville, or only design?

We design, write, build and host the site, and set up the contact form, titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema. That is what most local businesses need. If you need custom software, such as a customer login portal or an online store with a large catalog, that is a development project, and we will tell you so before you buy.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
